A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MFSC research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MFSC experiments on Meta-World, PyBullet’s Ant, DMControl, and CARLA, together with ablations and representation visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds camera ablations, a quantitative representation analysis, and experiments comparing MFSC with MOSER.

M1.justification: The CNN encoder, self-attention fusion, bisimulation objective, masked latent reconstruction, and dynamics models remain unchanged. Equations 4–10 and 13 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same procedures; the redrawn architecture diagram does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Appendix E.4 adds Open Window scenarios using each camera individually, extending observation-availability coverage beyond the earlier full-view and one-missing-view tests. Benchmark families remain unchanged; Cheetah Run and Walker Walk used in the new MOSER comparison already appeared in Table 4.

E2.justification: v2 adds MOSER as an evaluated comparator on Cheetah Run and Walker Walk in Appendix E.8 and Figure 18. Earlier comparator sets are retained. MV-MWM remains excluded from direct experiments, as explained in Appendix B.2.

E3.justification: The additions introduce individual-camera controls and evaluation of bisimulation loss and representation–state mutual information over training, using MINE for the latter. Existing hyperparameters and benchmark protocols are retained; the new MOSER comparison provides limited additional setting details.

E4.justification: Appendices E.4–E.5 add two focused Open Window analyses: whether all views outperform individual cameras, and how representation–state mutual information develops alongside bisimulation loss and return. Earlier component, noisy-view, loss-weight, and architecture analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix E.5 introduces MINE-based mutual-information estimation, adding a statistical estimation procedure. Existing confidence-interval and standard-deviation reporting and stated seed counts are unchanged. No increase in repeated runs or new significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: New results show multi-view Open Window performance exceeding each individual view, with View 3 worst; declining bisimulation loss accompanies increasing estimated mutual information. Figure 18 reports MFSC outperforming MOSER in both plotted tasks. Earlier tables and matched result curves are retained; the additions do not establish same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 explicitly adds that the unique fixed point is a π-bisimulation metric, while Definition 3.1 is reidentified with Castro (2020). This is a limited formal refinement: the operator formula, main assumptions, value-function bound, and Appendix A proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing bisimulation into MVRL, learning task-relevant fused representations, and improving robustness through masked latent reconstruction. Added experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: The missing-view discussion narrows improved convergence across most tasks to decent performance in some tasks. v2 also adds an explanation of color-removal sensitivity in contrastive and reconstruction methods, and interprets the new analyses through complementary views, occlusion, and alignment with ground-truth states.

D1.justification: v2 adds an MFSC project-code link in the abstract and implementation links for MINE and MOSER in the appendix. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware specifications, reward processing, and pseudocode are retained. These are additional access disclosures; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: v2 adds Castro (2020) and Wan et al. (2024), discusses MOSER’s viewpoint-selection approach, and changes the attribution of Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2 from Castro et al. (2021) to Castro (2020). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Changes include expanded bisimulation background, swapping the missing-view and noisy-view subsections, localized wording corrections, a shorter impact statement, acknowledgements, and updated affiliation/publication text. The overall narrative and section structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn; Figure 13 gains a camera-ablation panel; new Figures 14 and 18 display the quantitative analysis and MOSER comparison. Several existing figures are relocated or renumbered, while table structures and the overall document layout remain substantially the same.

improvement.justification: The camera ablation and quantitative representation diagnostic strengthen empirical support that previously relied more heavily on component ablations and visualizations. The MOSER comparison, code-access disclosures, and more cautious missing-view interpretation provide additional benefits. These gains are limited: the new analyses cover few tasks and provide sparse estimator and comparison-setting details, while the original method and principal results remain unchanged.
